course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
unit.description: Compare additive and multiplicative change, then build, compose, invert, and model with exponential and logarithmic functions, including residuals and semi-log plots.

firstTopic.title: Change in Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
firstTopic.summary: Sequences as functions of the whole numbers, arithmetic sequences with a common difference, geometric sequences with a common ratio, and the general term of each.

topics.title: Change in Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
topics.summary: Sequences as functions of the whole numbers, arithmetic sequences with a common difference, geometric sequences with a common ratio, and the general term of each.

topics.title: Change in Linear and Exponential Functions
topics.summary: Linear functions as the real-number version of arithmetic sequences, exponential functions as the real-number version of geometric sequences, and how to tell additive change from multiplicative change.

topics.title: Exponential Functions
topics.summary: The general form f(x) = abˣ, its initial value and base, exponential growth and decay, why exponential functions have no extrema or points of inflection, and their end behavior.

topics.title: Exponential Function Manipulation
topics.summary: The product, power, and negative exponent properties, unit-fraction exponents as roots, and how horizontal translations and dilations of exponential functions become vertical dilations and changes of base.

topics.title: Exponential Function Context and Data Modeling
topics.summary: Recognizing proportional growth in data, building an exponential model from a ratio and initial value or from two points, the natural base e, growth factors and percent change, and using equivalent forms to answer questions in context.

topics.title: Competing Function Model Validation
topics.summary: Comparing linear, quadratic, and exponential models for the same data, residuals and residual plots, judging whether a model is appropriate, and how errors show where a model underestimates or overestimates.

topics.title: Composition of Functions
topics.summary: Evaluating f ∘ g from tables, graphs, and formulas, why composition is not commutative, the identity function, building f(g(x)) analytically, and decomposing a function into simpler functions.

topics.title: Inverse Functions
topics.summary: When a function is invertible, how an inverse reverses input-output pairs, composition with the identity function, domains and ranges of inverses, reflecting a graph over y = x, and finding an inverse analytically.

topics.title: Logarithmic Expressions
topics.summary: What log_b c means, evaluating logarithms with and without technology, the common logarithm, and logarithmic scales.

topics.title: Inverses of Exponential Functions
topics.summary: The general form of a logarithmic function, how logarithmic growth reverses exponential growth, log_b x and bˣ as inverse functions, and reflecting graphs and ordered pairs over y = x.

topics.title: Logarithmic Functions
topics.summary: The domain, range, vertical asymptote, and end behavior of logarithmic functions, why they have no extrema or points of inflection, and recognizing a logarithmic pattern after an additive transformation.

topics.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
topics.summary: The product, power, and change of base properties for logarithms, the natural logarithm, and how horizontal dilations of logarithmic functions become vertical translations and dilations.

topics.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
topics.summary: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities with properties and inverses, checking for extraneous solutions, rewriting exponential expressions with logarithms, and finding inverses of transformed exponential and logarithmic functions.

topics.title: Logarithmic Function Context and Data Modeling
topics.summary: When a logarithmic model fits, building one from a proportion and a zero or from two points, transformations and logarithmic regression, the natural logarithm in models, and using the model to predict and solve.

topics.title: Semi-log Plots
topics.summary: Semi-log plots with a logarithmically scaled y-axis, why exponential data appear linear on them, and the linear model log_n y = (log_n b)x + log_n a that comes from y = abˣ.
